chunks: Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from Abdullah ibn al-Qaddah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said to a man: 'Did you become a fasting person this morning?' He said, 'No'. He (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Have you fed a poor person?' He said, 'No'. He (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'So return to your family, for it is charity from you upon them'.
ai.seo_question: What is the significance of returning to one's family as charity in Islam?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, the Prophet (SAWW) instructs a man who is neither fasting nor feeding the poor to return to his family, framing marital intimacy as a 'charity' (sadaqah) that fulfills one's spiritual and physical duties. This reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on rejecting extreme asceticism (rabbaniyya) by integrating worship with natural human needs, thereby validating sexual relations within marriage as an act of worship rather than mere indulgence. The narration underscores the balance (mizan) in Shia jurisprudence, where fulfilling conjugal rights is elevated to the status of sadaqah, ensuring that neglecting family life does not become a form of spiritual neglect.
